preamble: Denasalization of the bilabial nasal [m] to the labio-velar glide [w] keeps the lip closure gesture as rounding but loses nasality and full closure. In the Mandara group of Central Chadic, Proto-Central Chadic *m became w in word-final position, and in the common ancestor of the Wandala and Dghwede subgroups also word-initially before a vowel; elsewhere in Central Chadic *m is stable.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Central Chadic to Proto-Mandara (Mandara, Glavda, Podoko)

examples.to: Proto-Mandara *jɨwɨ; Mandara (Wandala) yawe, Glavda iyuw, Podoko yəwa
examples.note: Groups outside Mandara keep the nasal: Mafa, Mofu, Maroua, Sukur jam, Margi jimi, Lamang imi.
Word-final *m → w is regular in Proto-Mandara.
Compare Margi and Maroua mal, Mofu amal.
Word-initial *m → w before a vowel; Podoko does not share this extension.

sources: Gravina, R. (2014). The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: The Reconstruction of the Phonology and Lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the Linguistic History of the Central Chadic Languages. https://www.lotpublications.nl/Documents/375_fulltext.pdf
